Author: Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
Bench: Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Cheekati Manavendranath Roy
 Writ Petition No.3219 of 2023
Order:

-
This Writ Petition for a mandamus is filed to declare the action of respondents in proposing to demolish the private property of the petitioners bearing D.No.13-6-572 covered by T.Sy.No.4063,
4064, 4065 in Peddakappu Layout, Tirupathi, without issuing any notice to the petitioners and without following due process of law by initiating the process contemplated under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short "the Land Acquisition Act, 2013") as illegal and consequently sought direction to the respondents not to demolish the house of the petitioners without following due process of law.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Municipal Administration & Urban Development appearing for respondent No.1 and Sri Suresh Kumar Reddy Kalava, learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
3.
The fact that the petitioners are the absolute owners of the house bearing D.No.13-6-572 in Peddakappu Layout of Tirupathi is not disputed by the respondents.

The grievance of the writ petitioners is that without following due process of law as contemplated under the Land Acquisition Act, 2013, that the respondents are making an illegal effort to demolish the house of the petitioners for public purpose of widening the road without following the due process of law.
It is stated that the respondents have already given marking for demolition.

4. Learned Standing Counsel for the 2nd respondent, on written instructions, would submit that there is a proposal to widen the road and for the said purpose, a survey was made for the purpose of widening the road to 60 ft. and for the said purpose, the survey was made to ascertain whether the property in question is required for the purpose of widening the said road and no decision is yet taken by the respondents to acquire the property of the petitioners and he would submit that if at all the house of the petitioners is required for public purpose of widening the road that the respondents would follow due process of law as per G.O.Ms.No.223, Municipal Administration & Urban Development Department, dated 09.07.2018.
He has also placed the written instructions received by him to that effect on record.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that it is stated in the written instructions that they will only offer TDR bonds which is not acceptable to the petitioners and if at all the house of the petitioners is acquired for any public purpose of widening the road that they have to follow the procedure contemplated under the Land Acquisition Act, 2013.
6.

Therefore, in the said facts and circumstances of the case, recording the aforesaid submission made by learned Standing Counsel based on written instructions which are placed on record, the Writ Petition is disposed of with a direction to the respondents to follow the due process of law as contemplated under the Land Acquisition Act, 2013, to acquire the house of the petitioners for public purpose of widening the road, if at all the same is required for the said purpose.

Till the said process is initiated as contemplated under the aforesaid Act and till the property is acquired by due process of law, respondents are directed not to take any steps for demolition of the house in question.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, in the Writ Petition, shall stand closed.
